messages:
jon: proposing a lightweight schema extension for console telemetry storage: add compute_tier (enum) and per-tenant retention_days on route_metrics so we can enforce tiered storage and show exact retention in the UI.

maria: curious — why not just keep using labels/envelope fields we already have?

jon: two reasons: labels are messy for query planning and we need a deterministic partitioning key for archive vs hot. compute_tier will be an explicit column (hot, standard, cold). retention_days makes billing and admin controls straightforward.

tara: migration / migration cost? we have billions of rows. can't rewrite the table in one go.

jon: plan is additive-only: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN compute_tier TEXT NULL, ADD COLUMN retention_days INT NULL. initial default semantics = fallback to global TTL. then an async backfill that updates rows in batches. no table rewrite, no blocking exclusive lock.

kevin: adding columns can still bork query plans. any plan to avoid creating a full new partitioning immediately?

jon: yes. short-term: no partition change. long-term: create month+compute_tier partitions for archive shards and route recent 30d into hot partition. dashboards will hit a MV aggregated by (route_id, day, compute_tier) so reads are stable during migration.

maria: can you paste the rough DDL and the backfill sketch for infra review? also need a checklist for safety.

jon: DDL sketch:

ALTER TABLE route_metrics ADD COLUMN compute_tier TEXT NULL;
ALTER TABLE route_metrics ADD COLUMN retention_days INT NULL;

-- backfill (throttled):
-- UPDATE route_metrics SET compute_tier='standard', retention_days=30 WHERE compute_tier IS NULL LIMIT 50000;

Backfill will be an idempotent, rate-limited job run by eng-platform workers. We'll instrument p99 write latency and auto-throttle.

tara: consumers that read telemetry from Kafka/enrichment layer? joins downstream may break if compute_tier only lives in storage.

jon: we'll write compute_tier at the enrichment stage for new events. For historical rows, we won't change upstream event envelopes. For downstream consumers that need compute_tier, we'll emit a small compatibility topic message when enrichment assigns a tier (opt-in). Legacy consumers keep working.

kevin: how will we avoid double-counting in analytics while backfill is partial? mixed old/new rows could affect aggregates.

jon: MV will dedupe on route_metric_id and prefer rows with retention_days set. ingestion/update will update updated_at. MV logic: SELECT DISTINCT ON (route_metric_id) * ORDER BY updated_at DESC. Aggregations will read MV.

maria: what about backup/restore and rollback safety? if we restore an old snapshot without these columns, app code must tolerate it.

jon: deploy phases: 1) Add columns (code reads with safe defaults) 2) Start enrichment writing compute_tier for new events + dualwrite path via view for safe rollbacks 3) Backfill gradually 4) Switch dashboards to read new MV 5) Introduce partitioning and archive flow. At each phase app is tolerant of missing data.

tara: who's owning backfill windows and throttling SLAs? eng-platform or eng-infra?

jon: eng-platform owns orchestration and per-tenant quotas. eng-infra helps reserve low-IO maintenance slots. SLA for backfill: max 10k updates/sec globally, auto-pause if db p99 write latency > 250ms.

kevin: monitoring and alerts? need progress, failure, and planner regression visibility.

jon: agreed. expose metrics: rows_updated_total, rows_updated_per_tenant, backfill_eta_seconds, rows_failed_total. Create console dashboard tile for percent migrated per tenant and an alert: if any tenant ETA > 48h and tenant data > 1TB, pause and pager owners. Also track EXPLAIN p99 for key queries pre/post.

maria: archive format? cold storage expectations? retention-driven compaction?

jon: archive to S3 as partitioned Parquet by month and compute_tier. Store a lightweight index in metadata-store with (tenant, month, compute_tier, s3_path). Cleanup job will either tombstone or move rows to archive depending on retention policy. Archived months won't be served in the interactive console; retrieval is async.

kevin: can we add a small canary? pick 5 tenants (mix small and mid) and run enrichment + backfill for 48h, validate dashboards and billing counters.

jon: yes. canary plan: 5 tenants, 2-day run. validation: query parity between old and new MV, sampling of joins, billing delta < 0.1%. If canary passes, scale up with staged tenant cohorts.

tara: migration ownership matrix? need clear owners for runbook steps and QA.

jon: eng-platform: schema + backfill orchestration + MV creation. eng-infra: maintenance windows and DB capacity. eng-ml: help with query/perf testing for heavy aggregations. product/console: UI changes to show retention_days and compute_tier controls. security/compliance: approve retention semantics.

maria: add note for auditors: retention_days is authoritative for stored window; older backups may still contain rows outside retention. we need a small doc for compliance.

jon: will do. timeline: get PR for add-columns + runbook by EOD tomorrow. Deploy column-add next week (non-blocking). Backfill + enrichment to run over 2 weeks with canary first 48h.

ingest-bot: scheduled job created: "compute-tier-backfill" start=3267900000 throttle=10000rps owner=eng-platform

kevin: nice. also add an alert if backfill failures exceed 0.1% of processed rows for any tenant.

tara: once runbook lands i'll review and stamp. :thumbsup:
